sources.fact: 60 seconds of mineral oil exposure caused about a 90% decrease in latex condom strength (burst volume); baby oil and Vaseline Intensive Care lotion contain mineral oil
Most condoms come lubricated in the wrapper; adding lube helps keep them from breaking; water-based or silicone lube is safe with any condom; don't use anything with oil
Oil-based lubricants including massage oil, hand lotion, coconut oil and Vaseline can cause condoms to break
Do not use oil-based lubricant with latex condoms; use water-based or silicone-based lubricant

post.instagram_caption:
Baby oil can wreck a condom in 60 seconds 😳

Most condoms already come with lube in the wrapper, and adding more water-based or silicone lube is fine (it can even help stop breaks). But in one lab test, 60 seconds of mineral oil, found in baby oil and many lotions, cut latex condom strength by about 90%.

With latex condoms: no Vaseline, no lotion, no coconut oil.

Sources: Contraception journal (1989), Planned Parenthood, Bedsider, NHS.
